narrative: An employee's hand was pulled into the rollers of a laminator machine during a cleaning cycle, resulting in an amputation to their right index fingertip.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery during maintenance, cleaning
notes: cleaning cycle may need the rollers to run; then guarding is the primary

narrative: On June 10, 2024, an employee was grinding mulch in a tub grinder. A front end loader was unloading mulch into the tub grinder and ran over his ankle, breaking it and also causing a hairline fracture to his pelvis. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
event: Pedestrian struck by vehicle in nonroadway area  unspecified
notes: Front-end loader is not a powered industrial truck under 1910.178; struck-by hazard in general industry is typically cited under General Duty Clause 5(a)(1)

narrative: An employee suffered compression fractures to two back vertebrae while removing luggage from an overhead rack on a bus. She was hospitalized.
event: Overexertion in lifting-single episode
notes: Overexertion lifting injury; covered by General Duty Clause rather than a specific Part 1910 standard

narrative: An employee was waiting to offload a steel bar following a filament strand on a winder machine. His right index finger contacted the rotating section of the machine and was amputated above the knuckle. The injury required surgery.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery during regular operation

narrative: An employee was walking down the stairway and tripped. The employee sustained a fractured ankle.
event: Other fall to lower level, unspecified
notes: Narrative does not specify whether trip was due to stair defect/handrail (1910.25 / 1910.28(b)(11)) or surface hazard (1910.22(a))

narrative: An employee was walking on uneven pavement, lost their balance, and fell. The employee was hospitalized with a broken knee and clavicle.
event: Fall on same level  n.e.c.
notes: Uneven pavement/surface irregularity on walking-working surface

narrative: A temporary employee was operating a magnetic crane to pick up and move a 6000-pound sheet of metal when the metal fell and struck the employee's left foot, fracturing the fourth and fifth digits.
event: Struck by object falling from vehicle or machinery-other than vehicle part
notes: Overhead/magnetic crane load-handling failure; 1910.136 (foot protection) also relevant

narrative: An employee was working on a mobile conveyor system when his thumb got caught and injured.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery, unspecified
notes: Narrative does not specify whether employee was operating or servicing/cleaning the conveyor (if servicing, 1910.147 would apply)

narrative: An employee was on a work platform placing a tarp on a mulch trailer when the employee fell approximately 10 feet to the ground, suffering a head injury.
event: Other fall to lower level 6 to 10 feet

narrative: An employee was using a wheel cutter to cut rebar. The employee's glove was caught in the feed of the cutter, resulting in amputations to their left little and ring fingers.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery during regular operation
notes: Cutting metal rebar (not woodworking, so 1910.213 does not apply); general machine/point-of-operation guarding 1910.212 applies

narrative: An employee in the welding training booth was working to back gouge a weld on a 5mm plate. While grinding, the gouger high-centered and walked over the plate striking and severely lacerating the employee's left thumb.
event: Struck by running powered equipment  irregular movement, kick back
nature: Cuts, lacerations, punctures without injury to internal structures
notes: Portable grinder/gouger kickback during weld back-gouging; 1910.243(c) covers portable abrasive wheel tools (vs 1910.215 for stationary grinders)

narrative: An employee was operating a 55-gallon drum mixing machine when his hoodie got caught in the auger pulling him into the machine. He was able to free himself as the belt broke on the auger. The employee then fell to the ground and had a seizure. The employee sustained contusions and two broken ribs.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery during regular operation
source: Metal, woodworking, and special material machinery, n.e.c.
body_part: Chest, except internal location of diseases or disorders

narrative: An employee was operating a riding pallet jack when it struck a charging station. The employee's leg was caught between the rack of the charging station and the pallet jack and fractured.
event: Collision with stationary object, nonroadway

narrative: An employee was walking back to her work station. She tripped over the corner of a wooden pallet and fell to the ground sustaining injury to a knee and tendon.
event: Fall on same level due to tripping over an object

narrative: An employee was monitoring a cutter machine (back cutter) when the blade came up and caught her fingers. The employee sustained amputations of the tip of her left thumb and her left index fingertip. Shields (guards) were in place at the time.
event: Caught, entangled in running powered equipment  normal operation
notes: Shields were in place but did not prevent fingers from reaching the point of operation

narrative: An employee was working on a printing machine when their hand became caught in the machine. The employee sustained a fractured metacarpal, torn tendons, and a dislocated wrist.
event: Struck by running powered equipment  unspecified
notes: Narrative does not specify whether employee was operating or servicing/cleaning the printing machine

narrative: An employee was tightening a loose bolt that had allowed the steel back in a vertical hydraulic cylinder to loosen. The steel back closed on the employee's left hand, amputating it. He was hospitalized.
event: Contact with objects and equipment, unspecified
notes: Servicing/tightening bolt on hydraulic cylinder without isolating/blocking stored energy

narrative: An employee was making copies when he tripped and fell against another copier, breaking his hip.
event: Fall on same level due to tripping, unspecified
notes: Narrative does not specify what caused the trip (floor condition vs. object vs. misstep)

narrative: An employee was bitten by a spider while sitting at a computer. The employee developed an infection.
event: Bites and stings, unspecified
nature: Poisoning, toxic, noxious, or allergenic effect, unspecified
notes: Spider bite while sitting at a computer; no specific Part 1910 standard applies

narrative: An employee was working on a flour mill to remove a bolt using a breaker bar with a socket on end. The socket slipped off the nut and struck an unguarded moving belt. The breaker bar came back, hit the employee in his jaw and broke it.
event: Injured by slipping or swinging object held by injured worker
notes: Servicing/removing bolt while belt was running (1910.147), plus explicit unguarded moving belt (1910.219)

narrative: A piece of metal fell off of a roof that was being worked on and struck an employee on his left leg, causing a laceration between his ankle and his calf.
event: Struck by falling object or equipment, n.e.c.
notes: Falling object hazard from roof work; 1910.28(c) covers protection from falling objects (toeboards, canopies, barricades)

narrative: An employee was struck by a lower roller from a feeding machine. The employee was feeding cloth and rubber from the back of the machine. Tension built up and caused the roll to swing out from the machine. The employee sustained multiple injuries, which led to hospitalization: internal injuries, possible right arm fracture, three broken right-side ribs, and 6-inch laceration to right abdomen.
event: Struck by swinging or slipping object, other than handheld, n.e.c.
source: Metal, woodworking, and special material machinery, unspecified
notes: Roller swung out under tension while feeding cloth and rubber; general machine guarding/containment 1910.212

narrative: At 2:50 p.m. on March 2, 2022, an employee fell into a 24-inch slitter machine. The machine's slitter knives and slitter head amputated the employee's left hand.
event: Fall, slip, trip, unspecified
notes: Fell into slitter machine and amputated hand on slitter knives; both machine guarding (1910.212) and fall protection above dangerous equipment (1910.28(b)(6)) apply

narrative: An employee was returning from their break when the rags in his back pocket contacted a nearby stove heater. The rags caught on fire and spread to the employee's clothing. He sustained third-degree burns to the left and right buttocks.
event: Nonstructural fire, n.e.c.
source: Brooms, mops, and other cleaning tools
nature: Third or fourth degree heat (thermal) burns
notes: Unclear if rags contained flammable liquids (1910.106) or if stove heater lacked guarding/clearance (General Duty)

narrative: An employee was in the process of putting pipe into a machine when a clamp caught his left index finger and removed his fingertip. The employee was treated at the hospital and released.
event: Caught in running equipment or machinery during regular operation
